values.note: Every site must be reserved on recreation.gov; no first-come camping. Stays are limited to 6 nights April 1 - August 31 and 13 nights (14 days) September 1 - November 30. A site must be occupied within 24 hours of the first reserved day and not left unattended for more than 24 hours, or it may be cancelled. Up to 10 people and 2 vehicles a site.

note: BLM (Kremmling Field Office) campground and river access on the Colorado River beside the hamlet of Radium, off Trough Road (the Colorado Headwaters Byway) via Radium Road / County Road 11; no parking along narrow Radium Road. Two boat ramps and day-use shade shelters; four of the sites are walk-in tent sites. Radium Warm Springs is reached from the Warm Springs Road trailhead, not from the campground. No cell service without a booster. --Claude
summary: BLM page + recreation.gov: confirmed no hookups, reservable on recreation.gov, $25, phone 970-724-3000. Changed count 12 -> 16 (BLM: 16 single sites, 4 of them walk-in), max_rig_ft 80 -> 30 (the 80 is the pull-through driveway length; BLM figures 'small trailers' at 5-13 and 30 ft or less at 14-16). Added pull-throughs, no drinking water, vault toilets, season April 1 - November 30, reservation-only with the 6-night (Apr-Aug) limit, booking season. Note rewritten.
flags: Length: 'Campsites 5-13 have pull through parking areas and can typically fit one to two vehicles and small trailers. Campsites 14-16 have pull in parking and is 30 feet in length or less.' (recreation.gov/BLM). The stored 80 was the catalog's pull-through driveway length; recorded 30, the only figure given. The 'small trailers' wording at 5-13 has no figure, and 14-16 take up to 30 ft, so a 23-ft rig fits.
Count: the BLM says 16 single sites; 4 (sites 1-4) are walk-in tent sites with parking for one vehicle and no trailer, so 12 take a vehicle at the site. Recorded 16.
Max stay: 6 nights April 1 - August 31, 13 nights September 1 - November 30. Recorded 6; the fall figure is in booking.note.

Waterfront riverview confirmed (no change): on Esri imagery the drive-in sites nearest the river (16, 5) sit ~30 m from the Colorado behind a band of riparian willows, walk-ins 1-2 ~25-40 m, and the rest 60-200 m back across sage meadow. A view, not riverfront.
Pin 39.95136,-106.55598 (the recreation.gov facility point) is on the entrance road ~150-200 m north of the site loop (catalog centroid ~39.9497,-106.5557). OK.
Access: neither page says anything about Trough Road's surface or RV suitability; no RV/4WD wording.
